texto.@es: Con nombres incontables (**milk**) y contables en plural (**apples**), **some** suele aparecer en afirmativas: **There is some milk. There are some apples.**
texto.@en: With countless names (**milk**) and plural (**apples**) accounting, **some** usually appears in affirmations: * * There is some milk. There are some examples. * *

texto.@es: **Any** es lo habitual en preguntas neutras y negativas: **Is there any milk? There isn't any milk. There aren't any apples.**
texto.@en: **Any** is the usual in neutral and negative questions: * * Is there any milk? There is not any milk. There aren't any examples. * *

texto.@es: En ofrecimientos y peticiones corteses también es común **some**: **Would you like some tea?** (¿Quieres un poco de té?) y **Can I have some water, please?** (¿Me da un poco de agua, por favor?).
texto.@en: In short offers and requests is also common **some**: **Would you like some tea?** (Do you want some tea?) and **Can I have some water, please?** (Can I have some water, please?).
